dedupe_keys.name: ggcmi global gridded crop model intercomparison simulation outputs agmip and isimip

description: The Global Gridded Crop Model Intercomparison is the global crop modelling initiative of the Agricultural Model Intercomparison and Improvement Project (AgMIP), run by its Ag-GRID initiative. It is coordinated from the Columbia University Climate School, NASA GISS and the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, and is tied into the agriculture sector of ISIMIP. It produces multi-model ensembles of gridded crop simulations. Phase 1 evaluated models against historical weather; Phase 2 was a sensitivity archive from 10 models used to train crop yield emulators; a 2020 study looked at regional nuclear war cooling. Phase 3, aligned with ISIMIP3, gives the largest ensemble of climate impact projections for agriculture, with 12 crop models on the AgMIP page (ISIMIP counts 15 under its ISIMIP3a/b protocol) and 5 CMIP6 climate models. Coverage is global and gridded. Access to Phase 3 outputs is free through the ISIMIP Repository and its API, where files are organised by crop, model, climate forcing, scenario, irrigation and variable (for example anthesis day for maize under full irrigation, annual per growing season). The ISIMIP3b records read carry the CC0 1.0 public domain dedication, and the Phase II archives are on Zenodo per model and crop under CC BY 4.0 (for example LPJmL rice: yield, biomass, planting and maturity day, irrigation water withdrawal and evapotranspiration). Caveats: results differ between models and depend on the harmonised management inputs, and Phase 3 is ongoing, with more teams still adding simulations. For simulation it gives climate-driven crop productivity projections for agricultural hazard exposure, adaptation and food-supply scenarios. Related catalogue records include the ISIMIP Repository, LPJmL, DSSAT, APSIM and MAgPIE.
